page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at up to 4.2 GHz. It is provisioned with 64.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Cache sizing includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. The CPU incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Local ephemeral storage is bundled as a 944 GB NVMe solid-state drive, enabling low-latency scratch disk operations without relying exclusively on remote attached volumes. In benchmark testing, the instance consistently exhibits mid-tier throughput across standard CPU, memory, and compression routines, posting a PassMark CPU score of 22224.0 and Geekbench single-core and multi-core ratings of 1778.0 and 10435.0, respectively. Memory throughput reaches 105.59 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 54.61 GB/sec for writes. The platform delivers strong results in text processing (Geekbench text score of 2519.0) and small-model language inference, achieving 292.48 tokens per second on 135M parameter text generation.

Without hardware GPU acceleration, this configuration provides cost-effective density for compute and memory balanced workloads requiring fast local scratch storage. Primary workload fits include enterprise relational databases, Redis key-value caching layers, static web serving, software build compilation, and data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of memory, driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz across 8 physical cores. Architecture features include 260 MB of L3 cache alongside Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction extensions. Storage capacity is supplied through an integrated 944 GB local NVMe SSD, eliminating external storage overhead for high-frequency disk operations. Benchmark results position the server in the middle tiers for general compute and memory bandwidth, while highlighting strong efficiency in text processing and small-scale language model token generation. With its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, high-speed local disk, and lack of dedicated GPU hardware, the D16ds_v6 is suited for database servers, intermediate caching tiers, continuous integration environments, and general enterprise application hosting.
